The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically provides sampling weights and replicate weights for variance estimation in the database. The factsheet itself does not specify which weight variable (e.g., student sampling weight or replicate weights) is applied in the displayed estimates, so the exact weighting implementation is not recoverable from the text provided. For analysts reproducing these estimates from microdata, the OECD PISA database documentation should be followed to apply the provided student weights and the appropriate replicate-weight procedure when estimating uncertainty.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet summarizes performance and equity-related patterns for 15-year-old students in the Philippines across mathematics, reading, and science. It reports descriptive benchmarks such as mean performance, proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2+ and Level 5/6), and trends between 2018 and 2022, including changes in gaps across the top/bottom parts of the score distribution. The factsheet also highlights within-country subgroup differences (e.g., gender gaps in mathematics and reading) and associations with socio-economic status (ESCS), including the share of variance in mathematics performance explained by ESCS. It further describes contextual indicators from student, school, and principal questionnaires (belonging, discipline, safety, parental involvement) and COVID-related learning experiences. The document does not present an original predictive ML model, and it does not report model performance metrics or an explicit PV/missing-data handling strategy for re-analysis; it instead relies on OECD’s established PISA scaling and reporting procedures.
